html:
Leopold II was king of Belgium from 1865 to 1909, and from 1885 to 1908 the personal owner of the Congo Free State, a colony he ran as his own business.

He wanted a colony for his small country, which had none. Working through a supposedly scientific and charitable society, he hired the explorer Henry Morton Stanley, who set up stations along the Congo River from 1879, among them Léopoldville, now Kinshasa. At the Berlin Conference of 1884 and 1885 the European powers accepted his claim to the Congo basin, on the promise of free trade and an end to slavery. He made deals with local powers such as the trader Tippu Tip, and his forces fought for Katanga, where they killed Msiri of the Yeke kingdom in 1891.

When the world wanted rubber for bicycle and car tyres, the state forced Congolese villagers to collect wild rubber; see Congo Free State rubber. Soldiers took hostages, burned villages and cut off hands. Millions died from violence, hunger and disease, though the exact number is unknown. Reports by missionaries, by the British consul Roger Casement and by the journalist E. D. Morel caused an international outcry. In 1908 Belgium took the colony from him as the Belgian Congo. At home he spent his Congo profits on grand buildings and parks.
sum: Leopold II was king of Belgium from 1865 to 1909, and from 1885 to 1908 the personal owner of the Congo Free State, a colony he ran as his own business.
